subject: ela
skillName: Describe words and phrases in stories

items.prompt:
Read the poem below.

Cat, cat, soft and fat,
Curled up warm beneath my hat.
Cat, cat, what is that?
Just a nap on a welcome mat.

Which two words at the ends of lines rhyme with each other?
items.answer: 'Cat,' 'fat,' 'that,' and 'mat' all rhyme with each other. They all end with the same -at sound.

items.prompt:
Read the poem below.

Fluffy foxes find their food,
Freely, fairly, feeling good.

What is the alliteration in this poem? Which letter does it start with?
items.answer: The alliteration is the repeating /f/ sound: fluffy, foxes, find, food, freely, fairly, feeling. Nearly every word in the poem starts with the letter F.

items.prompt:
Read the poem below.

Star light, star bright,
First star I see tonight,
Wish I may, wish I might,
Have this wish I wish tonight.

Find the rhyming words. Which words rhyme?
items.answer: 'Bright,' 'tonight,' 'might,' and 'tonight' all rhyme. They end with the same -ight sound.

items.prompt:
Read the poem below.

Rain, rain, go away,
Come again another day.
Rain, rain, go away,
Little Leo wants to play.

What is the repeated line in this poem?
items.answer: The repeated line is 'Rain, rain, go away.' It appears at the beginning of lines one and three.

items.prompt:
Read the poem below.

Bumblebee, bumblebee, buzz around,
Bumblebee, bumblebee, low to the ground.

What letter makes an alliteration at the start of the poem?
items.answer: The letter B makes the alliteration: Bumblebee, bumblebee, buzz. All three start with the /b/ sound.

items.prompt:
Read the poem below.

Hop on a frog, hop on a log,
Hop in the bog, under the fog.

Find the rhyming words in this poem.
items.answer: 'Frog,' 'log,' 'bog,' and 'fog' all rhyme. They end with the same -og sound.

items.prompt:
Read the poem below.

Over the ocean, over the sea,
Over the mountain, over to me.
Over the river, over the plain,
Over the rainbow, over again.

What is the repeated word at the start of each line? What does repeating it make you think of?
items.answer: The repeated word is 'Over.' It appears at the start of every line. Repeating it makes you think of something traveling a long distance, going over one thing after another.

items.prompt:
Read the poem below.

Sleepy, sleepy, time for bed,
Rest your little weary head.
Sleepy, sleepy, close your eyes,
Listen to the fireflies.

Find the rhyming pairs in this poem.

Read the poem below.

Drip, drop, drip, drop,
The leaky faucet won't stop.
Drip, drop, drip, drop,
From the bottom to the top.

How does the sound of 'drip, drop' match what the poem is about?
items.answer: 'Drip, drop' sounds like the actual noise a leaky faucet makes. The short, repeated sound words make the poem feel like the sound of dripping water.

items.prompt:
Read the poem below.

Nine neat notebooks on a shelf,
Nadia chose one for herself.

Find the alliteration. Which words are part of it?
items.answer: The alliteration is the /n/ sound: nine, neat, notebooks, Nadia. All four words start with the letter N.

items.prompt:
Read the poem below.

The snow falls soft, the snow falls slow,
The snow falls white on the world below.

Find two rhyming words in this poem.
items.answer: 'Slow' and 'below' rhyme. They both end with the -ow sound.

items.prompt:
Read the poem below.

I love the moon, I love the stars,
I love the planets, even Mars.
I love the night, I love the sky,
I love to watch the clouds drift by.

What phrase is repeated in this poem?
items.answer: The phrase 'I love' is repeated at the start of every line. It is used four times.

items.prompt:
Read the poem below.

Jumping James jumped over the jar,
Jumped so high he reached a star.

What letter makes alliteration in line one?
items.answer: The letter J makes the alliteration: Jumping, James, jumped, jar. All four words start with the /j/ sound.

items.prompt:
Read the poem below.

Up in the tree, up in the sky,
Up where the eagles and small sparrows fly,
Up where the breezes blow free,
Up is the place I long to be.

What is the repeated word at the start of each line?
items.answer: The repeated word is 'Up.' It begins every line of the poem.

items.prompt:
Read the poem below.

Owen sees an orange and oval-shaped moon,
Owen hopes summer will come back soon.

Find the alliteration in this poem.
items.answer: The alliteration is the /o/ sound at the start of words: Owen, orange, oval, Owen. The words Owen, orange, and oval all begin with the same vowel sound.
